JM-04: Exposed input::CursorInput and the crate-root CursorInput re-export.
CursorInput::new accepts either Payload or a fresh borrowed strict jmax_cursor::Cursor, Limits, and NumericPolicy, returning Result<CursorInput>.
Implemented EventInput for owned CursorInput and &mut CursorInput, supporting both the inspected payload-based endpoint call and borrowed-cursor execution.
The adapter declares complete input, consumes real cursor events, rejects incomplete input, propagates sticky syntax failures, and exposes EOF only at ScanStep::Finished.

EventInput now permits append-only decoded arena growth and reallocation. Execution reads the live decoded slice after every event, requires monotonic arena lengths, enforces current limits, and revalidates retained references against final owners.
Publication transfers the completed cursor payload and final decoded arena. A borrowed cursor is replaced with a fresh strict cursor during successful ownership transfer.
Request numeric policy is applied using the shared VM work budget in addition to compiled schema policy.
JM-02_JM-03_support: ValidatedProgram shares immutable CompiledProgram and ProgramIndexes through Arc, providing constant-cost Clone and automatic Send + Sync for the contained owned data.
Program indexes are built once after full image validation; VM execution performs no lowering or image decoding.
Added image::load accepting a borrowed or owned SchemaImage through Borrow<SchemaImage>, restoring and validating the complete canonical program.

Standalone version-two images retain the canonical schema in a bounded capsule after the key-name prefix, with a checked length and magic footer. Loading reconstructs all states, constraints, patterns, key strategies, slots, and policy, then compares the exact standalone image before issuing a witness.
PERF-04: Removed full-table validation from keys::lookup; keys::validate remains the explicit compile/load validation boundary.
Added lookup_unchecked_table with checked memory access and lookup_index returning the global key index directly.

Capped SWAR tables at eight candidates. Small PHF tables use one candidate probe; large or unsuccessful single-level tables use deterministic two-level perfect hashing with two hashes and one candidate probe.

Two-level tables have a linear-size primary directory, at most eight secondary slots per key in total, bounded seed searches, exact collision checks, and explicit resource errors instead of unbounded SWAR fallback.
Object dispatch derives the local seen-bit index by subtracting first_key from the returned global index, eliminating the image-key pointer scan.
ValidatedProgram::slot_for_field and table_state replace slot scans and object-table owner scans.
Selection IDs and duplicates are validated once into a budgeted slot bitset. Per-key capture membership is constant-time, with an allocation-free empty-selection fast path.
Removed the per-capture EmitSlot instruction scan. Canonical image validation establishes the operand mapping, and execution directly resolves the immutable indexed SlotSpec.
VM lookup work accounting now charges bounded probes and query bytes instead of full-table revalidation and a temporary full-domain bitmap.

compatibility: IMAGE_VERSION is now 2. Version-one images are rejected because they cannot carry complete standalone schema semantics. Regenerate persisted or generated images with the new compiler.
KeyStrategy adds BucketedPerfectHash and the wire codec adds strategy tag 2. External exhaustive matches must handle the new variant.

SchemaImage.key_bytes now consists of key names followed by the canonical capsule. Existing key spans remain valid; external validators must recognize the version-two suffix instead of requiring all bytes to belong to key names.
Raw keys::lookup no longer establishes structural validity of unrelated entries. Validate raw tables once or obtain a ValidatedProgram before using hot-path lookup.
objects::key and extract::selected now consume SelectionIndex; selected accepts a compiled slot index rather than a FieldId.
CompilerOptions.swar_threshold is capped at eight. Hash seed exhaustion for a larger table returns BudgetExhausted.
image::load must receive compiler policy and strategy options compatible with those used to produce the image.
ValidatedProgram::into_program moves uniquely owned data and clones data if the witness is shared, so mutating the returned program cannot invalidate other witnesses.

integration_handoff.owner: Facade task owning crates/jsonmax/src/lib.rs and endpoint.rs
integration_handoff.action: Store ValidatedProgram directly in CompiledSchema during compile_schema and load_schema. Borrow that stored witness for validate_payload and extract_payload. The inspected endpoint still discards the witness and calls image::load per request; those files are outside this task ownership.
integration_handoff.slot_lookup: Replace endpoint extraction slot iteration with program.slot_for_field(*field). VM entry already validates selections, so the separate facade check_selection call is optional.

integration_handoff.action: Retain the validated witness per schema or workload and update generated-image version handling and capsule ownership rules for version 2.

validation.method: Manual source inspection only, including the audit, endpoint signatures, cursor traversal/finalization APIs, ABI ownership records, compiler codec, and VM dispatch paths.
validation.reason: The task explicitly prohibited all build and check commands.
validation.claims: No compilation, runtime correctness, performance measurement, or tool-based verification is claimed.

complexity.key_lookup: O(key byte length), independent of object schema key count; at most eight SWAR candidates or one exact PHF candidate.
complexity.slot_lookup: O(1) using a field-indexed slot vector.
complexity.selection_membership: O(1) using the request slot bitset.
complexity.selection_preparation: O(slot_count / 64 + selected_field_count), skipped for an empty selection.

scope_note: Only the nine exclusively owned Rust files and this handoff report were written.
